definition_zh: 峡谷；深谷；海底峡谷；城市峡谷
definition_en: a deep narrow valley with steep sides, usually cut by a river; also a similar narrow passage between high walls
core_image: 河水在岩层里切出一条又深又窄的竖缝，两侧是几乎垂直的岩壁
scene: 河水在岩层里切出一条又深又窄的缝，站在边缘看不到底。 The canyon drops three hundred metres from rim to river.
sceneCN: 此处指「河流在岩层中切出的深窄峡谷」（第 1 个义项：两壁陡直、深度远大于宽度的谷）；句意为从崖缘到河面，这条峡谷垂直下落三百米。图中可辨识物件：垂直岩壁、谷底河流、崖缘、看不到底的深度。

pos.zh: 峡谷；深谷（两壁陡直）；海底峡谷；城市峡谷

collocations.zh: 城市峡谷（高楼夹出的街道）

senses.title: A deep narrow river-cut valley
senses.definition: a deep valley with steep rock walls, cut by a river over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 由河流长期切割而成、两壁陡直的深谷
senses.example: The canyon drops three hundred metres from rim to river.
senses.exampleCN: 从崖缘到河面，这条峡谷垂直下落三百米。
senses.why: Spanish cañón named a tube or pipe; the word pictures a narrow channel with walls, not a broad valley.
senses.whyCN: 西班牙语 cañón 原指管子；这个词勾勒的是一条有壁的窄通道，而不是宽阔的谷。

senses.title: The canyon country as a region
senses.definition: a district characterised by many deep canyons, often used in place names
senses.definitionCN: 以众多深峡谷为特征的地带，常用于地名
senses.example: The canyon country attracts geologists every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这片峡谷地带每年春天都吸引地质学家。
senses.why: One canyon becomes a landscape when many of them define a whole district.
senses.whyCN: 当许多峡谷共同定义一整片地区时，一条峡谷就变成一种地貌景观。

senses.title: A submarine canyon
senses.definition: a steep-sided underwater valley cut into the continental slope
senses.definitionCN: 切入大陆坡的陡壁海底谷
senses.example: Sediment flows down the submarine canyon after storms.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，沉积物沿海底峡谷向下流动。
senses.why: The same cutting process works under water, so the same word names the submerged form.
senses.whyCN: 同样的切割过程在水下也起作用，同一个词于是指被水淹没的那一版。

senses.title: An urban canyon
senses.definition: a street enclosed by tall buildings on both sides, studied for wind and heat effects
senses.definitionCN: 两侧被高楼夹住的街道，常被研究风与热效应
senses.example: The urban canyon traps heat until well after sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 这条城市峡谷把热量困住，直到日落后很久。
senses.why: Tall walls on both sides reproduce the geometry of a canyon, so city planning borrows the word.
senses.whyCN: 两侧高墙复制了峡谷的几何形状，于是城市规划借用了这个词。

senses.title: A narrow deep passage
senses.definition: a narrow gap between high walls, natural or artificial
senses.definitionCN: 高墙之间的狭窄缝隙，天然或人造皆可
senses.example: The trail squeezes through a canyon of broken rock.
senses.exampleCN: 小径从一条碎石夹成的窄缝中挤过去。
senses.why: Width and depth, not a river, are what the word really requires.
senses.whyCN: 这个词真正要求的是宽度与深度，而不是必须有河。

senses.title: A huge gap between positions
senses.definition: a very large separation between opinions, generations or groups
senses.definitionCN: 意见、代际或群体之间的巨大分隔
senses.example: A canyon separates the two sides of the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 一场辩论的两方之间隔着一道鸿沟。
senses.why: A deep gap in the ground becomes a deep gap in agreement: both are measured by distance across.
senses.whyCN: 地面的深缝变成意见上的深缝：两者都用「跨越的距离」来衡量。

senses.title: Attributive: of a canyon
senses.definition: used before a noun for the walls, rim or floor of a canyon
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，指峡谷的壁、缘或底
senses.example: Canyon walls record millions of years of rock layers.
senses.exampleCN: 峡谷岩壁记录着数百万年的岩层。
senses.why: The noun simply marks which part or feature of the landform is meant.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词只是标出所指的是地貌的哪个部分或特征。

senses.title: A canyon-like landform type
senses.definition: a class of landform in geology, defined by depth, wall steepness and narrow floor
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中按深度、壁陡度与窄谷底定义的一类地貌
senses.example: The survey mapped every canyon in the basin.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查标出了盆地内每一条峡谷。
senses.why: Science turns the everyday word into a measurable category with thresholds.
senses.whyCN: 科学把这个日常词变成带有阈值的可测量类别。

intro.en: Canyon is an American Spanish loan from cañón 'tube, gorge', built on Latin canna 'reed'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: canyon 借自美洲西班牙语 cañón「管、峡」，后者由拉丁 canna「芦苇」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin canna meant 'reed, cane' and, by extension, anything tube-like; it is a borrowing from Greek kanna, itself probably from an Asian source.
items.cn: 拉丁 canna 意为「芦苇、茎」，引申指任何管状物；它借自希腊语 kanna，而后者可能又来自亚洲某语言。

items.en: Spanish caño meant 'tube, pipe, channel'; the augmentative cañón named a large tube or a deep narrow passage.
items.cn: 西班牙语 caño 意为「管、管道、水道」；增大的形式 cañón 指大管子或深窄通道。

items.en: In the southwestern Spanish-speaking world cañón was applied to the deep river-cut valleys of the region, adding the landscape sense.
items.cn: 在西南部讲西班牙语的地区，cañón 被用于当地由河流切出的深谷，从而增添了地貌义。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the nineteenth century, first in accounts of expeditions in the American West.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪借入这个词，最早出现在对美国西部考察的记述中。

items.en: The submarine sense is twentieth-century oceanography; the urban sense comes from city climate studies after tall buildings changed street wind patterns.
items.cn: 海底义属于 20 世纪的海洋学；城市义来自高楼改变街道风况之后的城市气候研究。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the Spanish-to-English date is approximate, and the pre-Latin origin of Greek kanna cannot be established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：从西班牙语进入英语的年代为约数，希腊 kanna 在拉丁语之前的来源无法确立。

note.en: The first group holds words that differ from canyon by one or two letters; the second holds words for narrow steep valleys.
note.cn: 第一组是与 canyon 差一两个字母的词；第二组是表示狭窄陡壁谷地的词。

entries.definition: A rule, or an accepted list of texts; it ends in -on, with no y, and comes from Greek kanōn 'rule'.
entries.definitionCN: 规则，或被认可的一组文本；结尾是 -on，没有 y，来自希腊 kanōn「规则」。

entries.definition: A large gun; it has a doubled n and comes through French from Italian cannone 'large tube'.
entries.definitionCN: 大炮；有双写 n，经法语来自意大利 cannone「大管子」。

entries.definition: The plural of canyon; the -s marks number, not a new word.
entries.definitionCN: canyon 的复数；-s 标记数量，不是新词。

entries.definition: A common misspelling that adds an r; it is not an English word.
entries.definitionCN: 常见误拼，多了一个 r；它不是英语词。

entries.definition: A narrow steep valley, often with a river; it is usually narrower than a canyon and less associated with dry country.
entries.definitionCN: 狭窄陡壁的谷，常有河流；通常比峡谷更窄，也不那么常与干旱地区联系。

entries.definition: Low land between high sides; it is broad and gently sloping, while a canyon is narrow with steep walls.
entries.definitionCN: 两侧高地之间的低地；宽阔而坡缓，而峡谷窄且壁陡。

entries.definition: A small deep valley worn by running water; it is much smaller than a canyon and usually has soil slopes.
entries.definitionCN: 由流水冲蚀的小深谷；比峡谷小得多，坡面通常是土。

entries.definition: A deep opening in the earth, often with vertical sides; it stresses the void and the drop rather than a valley floor.
entries.definitionCN: 地面上的深裂口，常为垂直壁；强调空洞与落差，而非谷底。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Spanish route, the real compounds and the modern technical senses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的西班牙语路径、真实的复合词与现代技术义。

normal.en: Latin canna 'reed' gives Spanish caño 'tube', then cañón 'large tube'.
normal.cn: 拉丁 canna「芦苇」给出西班牙语 caño「管」，再成为 cañón「大管子」。

normal.en: The family runs canyon, canyons, canyon wall, canyon floor, canyon rim.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 canyon、canyons、canyon wall、canyon floor、canyon rim。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: deep canyon, canyon rim, submarine canyon, urban canyon.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 deep canyon、canyon rim、submarine canyon、urban canyon。

normal.en: A canyon is measured by depth and wall steepness, not by length.
normal.cn: 峡谷用深度与壁陡度衡量，而不是长度。

normal.en: A valley opens; a canyon cuts. The difference is the wall.
normal.cn: 山谷是敞开的，峡谷是切开的；差别就在那面壁。

abstract.en: Picture a knife cutting straight down through many coloured layers of cake.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刀垂直切穿许多层颜色分明的蛋糕。

abstract.en: Picture two glass walls so close that the sky becomes a narrow strip.
abstract.cn: 想象两面玻璃墙靠得很近，天空缩成一条窄缝。

abstract.en: Picture two people on opposite rims who can see each other but cannot reach each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人站在对面的崖缘，能看见彼此却走不到一起。

examples.en: The river has cut the canyon deeper by a few centimetres each century.
examples.cn: 这条河每个世纪都把峡谷再切深几厘米。

examples.en: Hikers must carry water because the canyon floor is much hotter than the rim.
examples.cn: 徒步者必须带水，因为谷底比崖缘热得多。

examples.en: The street forms an urban canyon that blocks the evening breeze.
examples.cn: 这条街形成一条城市峡谷，挡住了傍晚的微风。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「看（kan）+ 甬（yon）」—— 往下看，只见一条像甬道的深窄石缝 → 峡谷

root: 美洲西班牙语 cañón「大管子、深峡」← 西班牙语 caño「管」← 拉丁 canna「芦苇、茎」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep one geometry: a narrow slot with steep walls, cut by water, by cities or by disagreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一种几何：一条两壁陡直的窄缝，由水、城市或分歧切出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a deep vertical slot cut into layered rock, with two nearly parallel walls.
core.cn: 核心意象：在层状岩层中切出的深竖缝，两侧岩壁几乎平行。

branches.en: THE LANDFORM: the river-cut slot, the district it defines and the geological class.
branches.cn: 地貌：河流切出的窄缝、它定义的地区以及地质类别。

branches.en: UNDER WATER: the same slot forms on the continental slope.
branches.cn: 水下：同样的窄缝在大陆坡上形成。

branches.en: BUILT WALLS: streets and rock passages reproduce the geometry.
branches.cn: 人造的壁：街道与岩缝复制了这种几何。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: a deep gap in ground becomes a deep gap between positions.
branches.cn: 比喻：地面的深缝变成立场之间的深缝。

branches.en: THE PARTS: walls, rim and floor are named by the noun in attributive use.
branches.cn: 各个部分：壁、崖缘与谷底由该名词的定语用法命名。

intro.en: Canyon is a Spanish loan with a clear Latin base; English builds compounds on it rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: canyon 是西班牙语借词，拉丁基础清晰；英语主要在它上面造复合词，而非后缀派生。

latinIntro.en: Latin canna 'reed' underlies Spanish caño and cañón; Latin canalis 'channel' is a related derivative of the same stem, which is why canal appears in the wider family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 canna「芦苇」是西班牙语 caño 与 cañón 的基础；拉丁 canalis「水道」是同词干的相关派生词，这就是 canal 出现在更广词族中的原因。

items.structure: American Spanish cañón, from caño 'tube', from Latin canna
items.example: The canyon runs for fifty kilometres.
items.exampleCN: 这条峡谷延伸五十公里。

items.example: Three canyons open onto the plateau.

items.meaning: the steep side of a canyon
items.example: The canyon wall shows red layers.
items.exampleCN: 峡谷岩壁露出红色岩层。

items.example: The canyon floor is hot at midday.

items.meaning: the top edge of a canyon
items.example: We stood on the canyon rim.
The submarine canyon feeds a fan of sediment.
items.exampleCN: 这条海底峡谷供给一片沉积扇。

items.example: The urban canyon limits air flow.
items.exampleCN: 城市峡谷限制了空气流动。

items.example: Canyonlands cover most of the park.
items.exampleCN: 峡谷地貌占了公园的大部分。

items.example: The Latin word named a hollow stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词指中空的茎。

latinEntries.structure: canalis, canalis (m., third declension, from canna)

definition_zh: 数字的；数值的；用数字表示的；数量上的
definition_en: relating to numbers, or expressed by numbers rather than by words or symbols
core_image: 一面墙上钉满小格，每一格里只写一个数字，没有形容词，也没有描述。
scene: 实验报告不写“效果很好”，只列出一排测量值。 The report gives only numerical results.
sceneCN: 这里 numerical 是“以数字形式表示、与数值有关的”（第 2 个义项）；句意：报告只给出数值结果。

pos.zh: 数字的；数值的；用数字表示的；数量上的

senses.title: Belonging to numbers
senses.titleCN: 数字的：与数字本身有关
senses.definition: relating to numbers as such, or to the system of counting and calculation
senses.definitionCN: 与数字本身或计数与计算体系有关
senses.example: The keyboard layout follows a numerical system, not an alphabetical one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个键盘布局遵循数字体系，而不是字母体系。
senses.why: The adjective marks the domain: the subject is numbers, so questions of value, order, and amount all belong here.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出领域：主题是数字，因此值、顺序与数量的问题都归在这里。

senses.title: Expressed as a number
senses.titleCN: 用数字表示：不写形容词，只写数
senses.definition: given in the form of a number rather than a word or a symbol
senses.definitionCN: 以数字而非词语或符号的形式给出
senses.example: The rating is numerical, from one to ten, with no verbal comment.
senses.exampleCN: 评分是数值型的，从一到十，不附文字评语。
senses.why: Here the word contrasts forms of expression: the same fact could be said in words, but a numerical form allows counting and comparison.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词对比表达形式：同一事实可以用文字说，但数值形式便于计数与比较。

senses.title: A number attached to a quantity
senses.definition: the particular number that expresses the size of a quantity in stated units
senses.definitionCN: 在给定单位下表示某一量大小的具体数字
senses.example: The numerical value of the coefficient depends on the units chosen.
senses.exampleCN: 该系数的数值取决于所选单位。
senses.why: A quantity has a size, and numerical names the number that reports it; change the unit and the number changes while the quantity does not.
senses.whyCN: 一个量有大小，numerical 指的是报告它大小的那个数；换单位，数会变，量本身不变。

senses.title: Ordered by number
senses.titleCN: 按数字排序：一二三四排下去
senses.definition: arranged according to number rather than by name, date, or topic
senses.definitionCN: 按数字而非名称、日期或主题排列
senses.example: The files are stored in numerical order from 001 to 999.
senses.exampleCN: 这些档案按 001 到 999 的数字顺序存放。
senses.why: Numbers provide a sequence that needs no interpretation: once the rule is fixed, anyone can find where an item belongs.
senses.whyCN: 数字提供一种无须解释的次序：规则一旦固定，任何人都能找到某物该放哪儿。

senses.title: Strength in count, not skill
senses.titleCN: 数量优势：人多，而非更强
senses.definition: advantage that comes from having more people or units than an opponent
senses.definitionCN: 因人数或单位数量多于对手而取得的优势
senses.example: The defenders had numerical superiority but no better position.
senses.exampleCN: 防守方在人数上占优，但地形并不更好。
senses.why: In military and competitive settings, numerical compares counts rather than quality, and the word admits that quantity can decide even without skill.
senses.whyCN: 在军事与竞赛语境里，numerical 比较的是数量而非质量；这个词承认数量有时无须技巧也能决定胜负。

senses.title: Solved by calculation
senses.titleCN: 数值方法：用近似计算求解
senses.definition: describing methods that approximate solutions by repeated calculation rather than exact algebra
senses.definitionCN: 指通过反复计算逼近解，而非求出精确代数解的方法
senses.example: The weather model uses numerical methods to step the atmosphere forward.
senses.exampleCN: 天气模型用数值方法把大气状态一步步向前推进。
senses.why: When equations cannot be solved exactly, calculation replaces derivation; numerical marks that the answer is an approximation built from many small steps.
senses.whyCN: 当方程无法精确求解时，计算取代推导；numerical 标出答案是由许多小步凑出的近似。

senses.title: Data in number form
senses.titleCN: 数值数据：能进表格的那种资料
senses.definition: information recorded as measurements or counts and therefore open to arithmetic
senses.definitionCN: 以测量值或计数记录、因而可作算术处理的信息
senses.example: The study combined numerical data with interviews of the same families.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究把数值数据与对同一批家庭的访谈结合起来。
senses.why: Data becomes numerical when it has been given units and a scale, which is what allows it to be averaged, plotted, and tested.
senses.whyCN: 数据在被赋予单位与标度后才成为数值数据，也正因如此才能求平均、绘图与检验。

senses.title: Machine control by numbers
senses.titleCN: 数控：让机器照着数字走
senses.definition: describing the control of a machine by coded numerical instructions rather than by a hand-operated lever
senses.definitionCN: 指用编码数字指令而非手动操纵杆控制机器
senses.example: The workshop replaced its manual lathes with numerical control machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家车间用数控机床取代了手动车床。
senses.why: The word entered manufacturing because a path can be described as a list of coordinates; numbers then become the instructions a tool follows.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入制造业，是因为一条路径可以写成一组坐标；数字由此成为刀具遵循的指令。

intro.en: Numerical comes from Latin numerus, a number, through the adjective numericus and the English suffix -al. The same root gives numeral, numerous, and enumerate.
intro.cn: numerical 来自拉丁语 numerus“数字”，经形容词 numericus 与英语后缀 -al 构成。同一词根还给出 numeral、numerous、enumerate。

items.en: Numerus meant a number, a count, a measure, and also a rhythm or a place in a series.
items.cn: numerus 意为数字、计数、度量，也可指节奏或序列中的位置。

items.en: The verb meant to count or to reckon. It is the source of English enumerate, to count out one by one.
items.cn: 动词意为计数、结算。它是英语 enumerate（逐一点数）的来源。

items.en: The adjective meant full of numbers, hence numerous or many. English numerous keeps only the 'many' sense.
items.cn: 该形容词意为“充满数字的”，因而表示“众多”。英语 numerous 只保留了“多”的意思。

items.en: Later Latin numericus meant concerned with numbers. It passed into learned English as numeric and numerical.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 numericus 意为“与数字有关的”，作为学术词进入英语，形成 numeric 与 numerical。

items.en: Numerical entered English through mathematical writing, where it distinguished quantity from shape, word, or symbol.
items.cn: numerical 经数学写作进入英语，用来把“数量”与形状、词语、符号区分开。

items.en: Computing and engineering widened the word to numerical methods, numerical data, and numerical control, where numbers serve as instructions.
items.cn: 计算与工程把该词扩展到数值方法、数值数据与数控；在这些领域，数字成了指令。

note.en: The first group is the number family; the second compares adjectives that describe measurement and quantity.
note.cn: 第一组是 number 词族；第二组比较描述度量与数量的形容词。

entries.definition: a count or symbol; or to count. It is the base noun behind all these forms.
entries.definitionCN: 计数或数字符号；也可作动词表示计数。它是这些形式背后的基础名词。

entries.definition: a written symbol for a number, such as 7 or VII. It names the mark, not the quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 表示数字的书写符号，如 7 或 VII；命名的是符号，不是数量。

entries.definition: another form of numerical, now especially common in computing and keypads.
entries.definitionCN: numerical 的另一种形式，今多用于计算机与键盘语境。

entries.definition: measured by amount rather than by quality. It describes a method, while numerical describes a form.
entries.definitionCN: 以数量而非性质来衡量；描述方法，而 numerical 描述形式。

entries.definition: represented by discrete digits, especially in electronics. It is about encoding, not arithmetic.
entries.definitionCN: 以离散数位表示，尤指电子领域；关乎编码，而非算术。

entries.definition: relating to the collection and analysis of data. It uses numbers but adds inference.
entries.definitionCN: 与数据收集和分析有关；使用数字，但增加了推断。

entries.definition: using figures of speech rather than literal numbers or plain meaning. It is the opposite direction from numerical.
entries.definitionCN: 使用修辞格而非字面数字或本义；与 numerical 方向相反。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin numerus, number, plus -ical, 'relating to'. Numerical simply means number-related.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 numerus“数字”，加 -ical“与……有关”。numerical 就是“与数字有关的”。

normal.en: Numerus is number; -ical is related to. Numerical equals number-related, nothing more.
normal.cn: numerus 是数字，-ical 是“与……有关”。numerical 就是“跟数字有关”，没有别的。

normal.en: A numerical report shows a row of values instead of a sentence of praise.
normal.cn: 数值报告给出一排数值，而不是一句赞美。

normal.en: Numerical order is the shelf where 001 always comes before 002.
normal.cn: 数字顺序就是 001 永远排在 002 前面的那种书架。

normal.en: Numerical superiority counts people, not skill.
normal.cn: 数量优势数的是人，不是本事。

normal.en: In a workshop, numerical control means the tool reads numbers and moves.
normal.cn: 在车间里，数控意味着刀具读了数字就移动。

abstract.en: A numerical answer hides its units; without units, the number is only a shape.
abstract.cn: 数值答案把单位藏在背后；没有单位，数字只是一个形状。

abstract.en: What can be made numerical can be compared, and what can be compared can be managed.
abstract.cn: 能变成数值的东西就能比较，能比较的东西就能被管理。

abstract.en: The word promises precision, but an approximation done in numbers is still an approximation.
abstract.cn: 这个词许诺精确，但用数字做出来的近似终究还是近似。

examples.en: The committee asked for a numerical estimate, not a general impression of the crowd.
examples.cn: 委员会要求给出人数估计，而不是对人群的笼统印象。

examples.en: Numerical models disagree with each other mainly in how they treat clouds.
examples.cn: 各数值模型之间的分歧主要在于如何处理云。

examples.en: The old milling machine was converted to numerical control to cut curved parts.
examples.cn: 那台旧铣床被改装成数控设备，用来切削曲面零件。

dict_mnemonic.text: numer（数字）+ ical（的）——满脑子都是数字，就是“数值的”。

root: 源自拉丁语 numerus（数字、计数），经 numericus 与英语后缀 -al 构成，本义为“与数字有关的”；同根词还有 numeral、numerous、enumerate。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of numerical. All point to numbers, but the numbers play different roles: they can be the subject, the form of expression, the value of a quantity, a sequence, a count of people, a method of calculation, a kind of data, or instructions for a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: numerical 的八个义项都指向数字，但数字扮演的角色不同：它可以是主题、表达形式、某量的大小、排列次序、人数、计算方法、数据种类，或机器的指令。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall of small boxes, each holding a single digit, with no adjectives anywhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面墙分成许多小格，每格只放一个数字，没有任何形容词。

chain: NUMBERS BECOME DATA, METHODS, AND INSTRUCTIONS

branches.en: NUMBERS AS SUBJECT AND FORM: the domain of number, and the choice to express a fact in digits.
branches.cn: 数字作主题与形式：数字的领域，以及选择用数位表达事实。

branches.en: NUMBERS AS VALUE AND ORDER: the size of a quantity, and the sequence on a shelf.
branches.cn: 数字作值与序：量的大小，以及架上的排列次序。

branches.en: NUMBERS AS COUNT: superiority that comes from having more units than the opponent.
branches.cn: 数字作计数：因单位多于对手而形成的优势。

branches.en: NUMBERS AS METHOD AND DATA: approximation by calculation, and measurements open to arithmetic.
branches.cn: 数字作方法与数据：以计算求近似，以及可作算术处理的测量值。

branches.en: NUMBERS AS COMMAND: coordinates read by a machine tool.
branches.cn: 数字作指令：机床读取的坐标。

intro.en: Numerical is numerus plus the adjective suffix -ical. The family runs through number, numeral, numerate, and the prefix e- in enumerate.
intro.cn: numerical 是 numerus 加形容词后缀 -ical。词族包括 number、numeral、numerate，以及带前缀 e- 的 enumerate。

latinIntro.en: The base is numerus, number or count, with the verb numerare and the adjective numerosus. Latin also used numerus for rhythm and rank.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 numerus“数字、计数”，另有动词 numerare 与形容词 numerosus。拉丁语还用 numerus 指节奏与等级。

items.meaning: a count, a symbol, or a quantity
items.example: The number of applicants doubled in one year.
items.exampleCN: 申请人数量一年内翻了一倍。

items.meaning: a symbol used to write a number
items.example: Roman numerals use letters instead of digits.
items.exampleCN: 罗马数字用字母而非数位。

items.meaning: relating to numbers or expressed by them
items.meaningCN: 与数字有关的，或以数字表示的
items.example: The table gives numerical results for each trial.
items.exampleCN: 表格给出每次试验的数值结果。

items.meaning: in number or in numerical terms
items.example: The two groups were numerically equal.
items.exampleCN: 两个群体在人数上相等。

items.meaning: able to work with numbers; also to count
items.meaningCN: 会算数的；也可作动词表示计数
items.example: A numerate reader can check the totals quickly.
items.exampleCN: 会算数的读者能很快核对总数。

items.meaning: the number above the line in a fraction
items.example: In three quarters, three is the numerator.
items.exampleCN: 在四分之三里，三是分子。

items.meaning: to list items one by one
items.example: The report enumerates every source of error.
items.exampleCN: 报告逐项列出了每一种误差来源。

items.example: Numerous studies report the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: 众多研究报告了同样的模式。

items.example: The storm left innumerable branches on the road.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨在路面上留下数不清的树枝。

definition_zh: 防腐剂；保护剂；防腐的
definition_en: a substance added to food, wood or another material to prevent decay, or the adjective meaning 'serving to preserve'
core_image: 一小瓶透明液体倒进果酱罐里，罐外壁上的霉点立刻停住不动
scene: 这里指「防腐剂」。 The label says the bread contains no preservative.
sceneCN: 这里 preservative 是「防腐剂」（第 1 个义项：防止腐败的添加物）；句意：标签上写着这款面包不含防腐剂。图中可辨识物件：小瓶液体、果酱罐、停在半路的霉点。

senses.title: A substance against decay
senses.definition: a substance added to a product to stop it decaying or spoiling
senses.definitionCN: 加入产品中以防止其腐败变质的物质
senses.example: Nitrites are a common preservative in cured meat.
senses.exampleCN: 亚硝酸盐是腌肉中常用的防腐剂。
senses.why: The -ative suffix marks what does the work, so preservative is literally 'the thing that preserves'. The substance carries out the verb.
senses.whyCN: -ative 后缀标记“执行动作者”，所以 preservative 字面就是“起保存作用的东西”。物质在执行那个动词。

senses.title: Food additive
senses.titleCN: 食品添加剂中的那一类
senses.definition: a food additive whose function is shelf life rather than colour, texture or taste
senses.definitionCN: 食品添加剂中功能为延长保质期、而非调色调味的那一类
senses.example: Preservatives must be listed after the ingredients.
senses.exampleCN: 防腐剂必须列在配料之后。
senses.why: Regulation separates additives by function, and preservation is one function among several. The word becomes a legal category.
senses.whyCN: 法规按功能区分添加剂，保存是其中一项。这个词因此成为法律分类。

senses.title: Cosmetics and pharmacy
senses.titleCN: 化妆品与药品里的防腐
senses.definition: an ingredient that stops microbes growing in a cream, lotion or liquid medicine
senses.definitionCN: 阻止微生物在乳霜、洗液或药水中生长的成分
senses.example: Water-based creams need a preservative to stay safe.
senses.exampleCN: 水基乳霜需要防腐成分才能保持安全。
senses.why: Anything water-based can host bacteria. The preservative protects the user, not only the product.
senses.whyCN: 任何含水产品都可能滋生细菌。防腐剂保护的是使用者，不只是产品。

senses.title: Wood and materials
senses.definition: a treatment applied to timber or fabric to resist insects, fungus and rot
senses.definitionCN: 涂于木材或织物以抗虫、抗真菌与抗腐朽的处理剂
senses.example: The fence was dipped in a copper preservative.
senses.exampleCN: 栅栏在铜盐防腐剂中浸过。
senses.why: The word leaves the kitchen and enters building work, where the same enemies appear: water, fungi and insects.
senses.whyCN: 这个词离开厨房进入建筑，敌人却相同：水、真菌与昆虫。

senses.title: Adjective: preserving
senses.titleCN: 形容词义：有保存作用的
senses.definition: used as an adjective for something that tends to preserve, now mostly in fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词表示“有保存倾向的”，现多用于固定短语
senses.example: The preservative effect of salt was known before chemistry.
senses.exampleCN: 盐的防腐作用在化学出现之前就已被知晓。
senses.why: The same -ative ending can describe a tendency rather than name a substance, so the word doubles as an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -ative 结尾既可描述倾向，也可命名物质，所以这个词兼作形容词。

senses.title: Preservative-free claim
senses.definition: used in marketing phrases that promise no added preservative, sometimes with a shorter shelf life
senses.definitionCN: 用于承诺未添加防腐剂的营销说法，往往意味着保质期更短
senses.example: The preservative-free version costs twice as much.
senses.exampleCN: 不含防腐剂的版本价格翻倍。
senses.why: A negative phrase can carry as much meaning as a positive one: no preservative means the product must be used quickly.
senses.whyCN: 否定短语与肯定短语同样有信息量：没有防腐剂意味着产品必须尽快用完。

senses.title: Vaccine preservative
senses.definition: an antimicrobial added to multi-dose vaccine vials to prevent contamination between doses
senses.definitionCN: 加入多剂型疫苗瓶中以防剂量间污染的抗微生物成分
senses.example: Thimerosal was used as a preservative in some vaccines.
senses.exampleCN: 硫柳汞曾在一些疫苗中作防腐剂。
senses.why: Public health adds a new frame: the risk is contamination each time a vial is opened, so the substance guards the vial itself.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生加了新框架：风险在于每次开瓶的污染，所以该物质守护的是瓶子本身。

senses.title: Preservative versus additive
senses.definition: the class of additives defined by purpose, distinguished from colourings, emulsifiers and flavourings
senses.definitionCN: 按用途划分的一类添加剂，区别于着色剂、乳化剂与调味剂
senses.example: Not every additive is a preservative, though every preservative is an additive.
senses.exampleCN: 并非所有添加剂都是防腐剂，但所有防腐剂都是添加剂。
senses.why: Classification works by function. Preservation is one job in the additive toolbox, which is why the two words nest rather than overlap.
senses.whyCN: 分类按功能划分。保存是添加剂工具箱中的一项工作，所以两词是包含关系，而非重叠。

intro.en: Preservative is formed on Latin praeservare 'to keep safe beforehand' (prae- 'before' + servare 'keep safe') plus the suffix -ative, from Latin -ativus.
intro.cn: preservative 由拉丁 praeservare“预先保全”（prae-“在前”+ servare“保全”）加后缀 -ative（来自拉丁 -ativus）构成。

items.en: servare 'to watch over, keep safe' is the base of the family. Its further root is uncertain; the usual PIE *ser- reconstruction is debated and should be marked uncertain.
items.cn: servare“看守、保全”是词族的基础。其更深词根不确定，常见的原始印欧语 *ser- 重构有争议，应标“来源不确定”。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus servare gives 'to guard in advance'. The prefix explains why preservation begins before decay.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 servare 得“提前看守”。前缀解释了为何保存要在腐坏之前开始。

items.en: -ativus in Latin marks a capacity or an agent, as in 'serving to do'. English -ative keeps that double role, so a preservative can be a thing or a quality.
items.cn: 拉丁 -ativus 标记能力或施事，意为“用于做……的”。英语 -ative 保留这双重角色，所以 preservative 既可指物，也可指性质。

items.en: English records preservative first as an adjective meaning 'having the power to preserve', then as a noun for a substance.
items.cn: 英语最早把 preservative 记为形容词“有保存能力的”，随后作为物质名词使用。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries chemical preservatives expand with canning and long-distance food trade, and regulation follows.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，化学防腐剂随罐装与远距离食品贸易扩张，相关法规随之出现。

items.en: Late 20th century labelling turns the word into a consumer signal, with preservative-free claims on the front of the pack.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，标签让这个词成为消费信号，包装正面出现“不含防腐剂”的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the serv- stem or the -ative ending; the near-meaning group all protect something, but not all are substances.
note.cn: 形近组共享 serv- 词干或 -ative 结尾；近义组都起保护作用，但不都是物质。

entries.definition: the act or state of being kept safe. It names the process; preservative names the agent that does it.
entries.definitionCN: 保存的行为或状态。它命名过程，preservative 命名执行过程的物质。

entries.definition: to keep from decay. The verb is the action the substance performs.
entries.definitionCN: 保存；保护。它是该物质执行的动作。

entries.definition: favoring tradition and resisting change. It shares servare through conservare 'keep together', but means social caution, not decay prevention.
entries.definitionCN: 保守的。它经由 conservare“共同保存”共享 servare，但指社会态度上的谨慎，不是防腐败坏。

entries.definition: any substance added to a product for a purpose. A preservative is one kind of additive.
entries.definitionCN: 添加剂。指为某目的加入产品的任何物质，防腐剂是其中一种。

entries.definition: a substance that slows oxidation. It is a preservative working by one specific chemical route.
entries.definitionCN: 抗氧化剂。它通过特定化学途径起防腐作用。

entries.definition: a substance that kills microbes on the body. It protects health, while a preservative protects the product.
entries.definitionCN: 抗菌剂；消毒剂。它保护健康，而防腐剂保护产品。

entries.definition: a substance that keeps a product's structure or mixture from changing. It prevents separation rather than decay.
entries.definitionCN: 稳定剂。它防止结构或混合物分离，而非防止腐败。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: -ative marks the agent, so a preservative is the thing that does the preserving.
normal.cn: -ative 标记施事，所以 preservative 就是“做保存这件事的东西”。

normal.en: Food, cosmetics, wood and vaccines all use the word because all four can host microbes or rot.
normal.cn: 食品、化妆品、木材、疫苗都用这个词，因为四者都可能滋生微生物或腐烂。

normal.en: Preservative-free is a fixed label phrase and always implies a shorter shelf life.
normal.cn: 不含防腐剂是固定标签短语，总意味着保质期更短。

normal.en: The nesting is one-way: every preservative is an additive, but not every additive preserves.
normal.cn: 包含关系是单向的：所有防腐剂都是添加剂，但并非所有添加剂都起保存作用。

normal.en: The adjective use survives in preservative effect, where the word describes a quality rather than a bottle.
normal.cn: 形容词用法保留在“防腐作用”这类短语里，描述的是性质而不是一瓶东西。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands are held still by a drop of oil.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴油把钟表的指针按住不动。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed envelope that keeps air away from a photograph.
abstract.cn: 想象一只封好的信封，把空气挡在照片之外。

abstract.en: Picture salt crystals surrounding a fish, taking the water out before the microbes can use it.
abstract.cn: 想象盐粒包围一条鱼，在微生物利用水分之前把水抽走。

examples.en: The jam contains only fruit, sugar and one preservative.
examples.cn: 这种果酱只含水果、糖和一种防腐剂。

examples.en: Preservative-treated timber lasts far longer outdoors.
examples.cn: 经防腐处理的木材在户外耐用得多。

examples.en: Some preservatives are harmless in small doses and problematic in large ones.
examples.cn: 有些防腐剂小剂量无害，大剂量则有问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞泽沃提夫”音近 preservative：普普通通的东西先“则”住、再“沃”住水、最后“提”住不坏——加进去防腐败 → preservative 防腐剂

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前”+ servare“保全”（更深词源存疑）→ praeservare“预先保全”；praeservat- 词干 + -ative（拉丁 -ativus，表施事或能力）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe an agent that slows decay, and the differences come from where the decay would happen.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述“让腐坏变慢的施事”，差别在腐坏本来会发生在哪里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop that stops mould in its tracks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴让霉菌停住的液体。

branches.en: AGENT AND QUALITY: the noun names the substance, the adjective names its tendency, and both come from one suffix.
branches.cn: 施事与性质：名词命名物质，形容词命名倾向，两者出自同一后缀。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION: as an additive class, the word is defined by purpose rather than by chemistry.
branches.cn: 分类：作为添加剂的一类，它按用途而非化学成分定义。

branches.en: PROTECTING USERS: creams and multi-dose vials are guarded because they touch people.
branches.cn: 保护使用者：乳霜与多剂瓶被防护，因为它们接触人体。

branches.en: MATERIALS: wood and cloth meet the same enemies as food, so the same word serves.
branches.cn: 材料：木材与织物面对与食物相同的敌人，所以沿用同一个词。

branches.en: MARKETING: the negative label phrase turns absence into a selling point.
branches.cn: 营销：否定式标签把“没有”变成卖点。

intro.en: Preservative is the Latin stem preservat- plus -ative. The stem carries 'keep safe', and the suffix marks either the agent or the quality.
intro.cn: preservative 是拉丁词干 preservat- 加 -ative。词干携带“保全”，后缀标记施事或性质。

latinIntro.en: Latin servare 'keep safe' → praeservare 'guard beforehand' → praeservativus. English keeps the stem preservat- throughout the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 servare“保全”→ praeservare“提前看守”→ praeservativus。英语全族保留 preservat- 词干。

items.example: Preservation of the site is urgent.
items.exampleCN: 该遗址的保护十分紧迫。

items.meaning: a substance or quality that preserves

items.example: She is a preserver of old recipes.
Preserved lemons are common in North Africa.

items.exampleCN: 新鲜无花果几乎无法保存。

items.meaning: careful protection of nature or heritage
items.exampleCN: 保护团体反对这条公路。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 看守；保全（更深来源存疑）

definition_zh: 把材料切割、成形并装配成构件的过程；也指捏造、伪造之事
definition_en: the process of cutting, forming and assembling materials into a structure, or the act of inventing something false
core_image: 钢板上先画线，再被等离子弧切开，边缘打磨后吊到胎架上点焊，一块构件就这样从平板变成梁
scene: 加工车间里，钢板被等离子切割机切开，边角打磨后吊到胎架上点焊成梁。 Sheet-metal fabrication requires precise measurements.
sceneCN: 这里指金属板材的加工与成型过程（第 1 个义项：把材料切割、成形并装配成构件的过程）；句意：金属板材加工需要精确的测量。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「工匠制作」进入英语，义为「制造；捏造」
由「制造」加已然词尾构成，义为「制造的；捏造的」
由「制造」加施动词尾构成，义为「制造者、加工商」
由拉丁语「工坊、织物」进入英语，义为「织物、结构」
由「预先」加「制造」构成，义为「预制」
由「预制」加名词词尾构成，义为「预制加工」

senses.title: Cutting and forming metal
senses.definition: the industrial process of cutting, bending and welding material into finished parts
senses.definitionCN: 把材料切割、弯折并焊接成成品构件的工业过程
senses.example: The fabrication of the frame took four days in the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 框架的加工在车间里花了四天。
senses.why: The root verb means to make by a craftsman, so the noun names the making of a built object.
senses.whyCN: 词根动词意为工匠制作，因此这个名词指把物件做出来的过程。

senses.title: Assembly of parts into a whole
senses.definition: the joining of cut parts into a single structure or machine
senses.definitionCN: 把切好的部件连接成一个结构或机器
senses.example: Fabrication and erection are separate contracts on this site.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个工地上，加工与安装是两份分开的合同。
senses.why: Making a structure needs both cutting and joining, and the word covers the joined result as well as the cutting.
senses.whyCN: 造结构既需切割也需连接，这个词既指切割，也指连接后的成品。

senses.title: Inventing a false story
senses.definition: the act of inventing facts, an account or an excuse that is not true
senses.definitionCN: 编造不真实的事实、叙述或借口
senses.example: The whole rumour was a fabrication from a single anonymous post.
senses.exampleCN: 整个谣言只是从一个匿名帖子编造出来的。
senses.why: A thing made can be made without material, so the word extends from building objects to building lies.
senses.whyCN: 造物可以不用材料，于是这个词从造物件扩展到造谎言。

senses.title: Forging a document or evidence
senses.definition: the deliberate making of a false document, record or piece of evidence
senses.definitionCN: 有意制作虚假文件、记录或证据
senses.example: The court found the letter to be a fabrication.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭认定这封信是伪造的。
senses.why: False paper is also made by a maker, so the manufacturing word serves for deliberate forgery.
senses.whyCN: 假文件同样由制作者做出，因此制造词也用于有意的伪造。

senses.title: Semiconductor manufacturing
senses.definition: the sequence of deposition, etching and patterning that turns a wafer into chips
senses.definitionCN: 把晶圆变成芯片的沉积、刻蚀与图形化流程
senses.example: Wafer fabrication needs a clean room cleaner than an operating theatre.
senses.exampleCN: 晶圆制造需要比手术室更洁净的洁净室。
senses.why: Chip making is a highly controlled kind of making, so the general word names the whole factory process.
senses.whyCN: 芯片制造是高度受控的制造，因此这个泛称指整个工厂流程。

senses.title: Steel structure work
senses.definition: the cutting, drilling and welding of steel members in a fabrication shop
senses.definitionCN: 在加工车间对钢构件进行切割、钻孔与焊接
senses.example: The bridge's fabrication was checked against the shop drawings.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的钢结构加工对照车间图纸进行了检查。
senses.why: Steel is cut and joined away from site, and that shop work is the clearest industrial use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 钢在现场之外被切割与连接，这种车间工作是该词最清晰的工业用法。

senses.title: A made-up thing
senses.definition: a story, excuse or claim that has been invented and does not exist as described
senses.definitionCN: 被编造出来、并不如所述存在的说法、借口或主张
senses.example: His alibi was a fabrication with no supporting detail.
senses.exampleCN: 他的不在场证明是捏造的，没有任何细节支撑。
senses.why: The noun can name the false thing itself, not only the act of making it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可指虚假之物本身，而不只是编造的动作。

senses.title: A fabrication shop or trade
senses.definition: the workshop, business or trade that cuts and assembles material for construction
senses.definitionCN: 为建筑切割并组装材料的车间、企业或行业
senses.example: She learned welding in a small fabrication on the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 她在海边一家小型加工车间学会了焊接。
senses.why: The place where the work is done takes the name of the work, a common shift in trade words.
senses.whyCN: 干活的地方沿用工作的名称，这是行业词常见的转义。

intro.en: Fabrication comes from Latin words for a craftsman and his workshop; English first used it for making things and later for making things that are not true.
intro.cn: 「制造」来自拉丁语中表示工匠及其工坊的词；英语先用它指造物，后来也指造出不真实的东西。

items.en: Faber meant a craftsman, especially a smith or carpenter; it is the direct Latin source, while its deeper origin is uncertain and the link to a shaping root is only a suggestion.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语名词指工匠，尤指铁匠或木匠；它是本词的直接拉丁语来源，其更早来源存疑，与表示「塑造」之词根的关联仅为推测。

items.en: Fabrica named a workshop and also the craft or structure made there, and English fabric later narrowed to woven cloth.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语名词指工坊，也指在那里做出的手艺或结构；英语的「织物」后来缩小为编织布料。

items.en: Fabricare meant to make, build or shape something in a workshop, with no hint of deceit.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语动词指在工坊里制作、建造或塑造，完全没有欺骗含义。

items.era: LATIN FABRICATIO · FIRST RECORD DATE UNCERTAIN
items.en: Fabricatio named the act of making, and English fabrication kept that sense for metal, timber and stone work; the earliest English record of the borrowed noun is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语名词指制作的行为，英语的「制造」保留了用于金属、木材与石材工作的含义；英语借入这一名词的最早记录年代不确定。

items.en: From the idea of building a thing comes the idea of building a story, and by the eighteenth century fabrication could mean a lie.
items.cn: 从「造物」的观念衍生出「造故事」的观念，到十八世纪，这个词已可指谎言。

items.en: Engineering kept the honest sense for cutting and welding, while semiconductor work gave it a high-technology meaning.
items.cn: 工程保留了切割与焊接的诚实义，半导体工作又给了它一个高科技含义。

note.en: The first group shares the craftsman root; the second group separates making words from falsehood words.
note.cn: 第一组共享「工匠」词根；第二组区分制造词与虚假词。

entries.definition: To make or to invent falsely; the action behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 制造或编造；名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: Made, or invented in order to deceive.
entries.definitionCN: 已制造的，或为欺骗而编造的。

entries.definition: A maker or a person who invents false accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 制造者，或编造虚假说法的人。

entries.definition: Woven cloth or the structure of a building; the same root, narrowed.
entries.definitionCN: 织物或建筑的结构；同词根，词义缩小。

entries.definition: Making goods on a large scale by hand or machine; it stresses volume, not a single built member.
entries.definitionCN: 大规模手工或机器制造；强调产量，而非单件构件。

entries.definition: Putting finished parts together; fabrication also cuts and forms those parts.
entries.definitionCN: 把成品零件装在一起；目标词还包含切割与成形。

entries.definition: A false document made to deceive; narrower than the falsehood sense of the target.
entries.definitionCN: 为欺骗而做的假文件；比目标词的虚假义窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real fixed terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is the craftsman in his workshop, making what he is asked to make.
normal.cn: 词根是工坊里的工匠，按要求制作东西。

normal.en: The family runs fabricate, fabricated, fabricator, fabric, prefabricate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括制造、制造的、制造者、织物、预制。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: metal fabrication, fabrication shop, fabrication of evidence.
normal.cn: 固定搭配可标记它：金属加工、加工车间、伪造证据。

normal.en: The honest sense cuts and welds; the dishonest sense invents and forges.
normal.cn: 诚实义用于切割与焊接，不诚实义用于编造与伪造。

normal.en: Its test is material: a lie has no shop drawing.
normal.cn: 它的检验是物质性的：谎言没有车间图纸。

abstract.en: Picture a flat plate becoming a beam after one cut and one weld.
abstract.cn: 想象一块平板经过一次切割与一次焊接变成一根梁。

abstract.en: Picture a story assembled from spare parts that no supplier ever sold.
abstract.cn: 想象一个用从未有供应商卖过的零件拼成的故事。

abstract.en: Picture a signature drawn by a hand that never owned the name.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从未拥有该姓名的手画出的签名。

examples.en: Metal fabrication holds the tolerance better than site cutting.
examples.cn: 金属加工比现场切割更能保证公差。

examples.en: The report's key quotation turned out to be a fabrication.
examples.cn: 报告的关键引文结果是捏造的。

examples.en: He runs a small fabrication behind the railway yard.
examples.cn: 他在铁路场后面经营一家小型加工车间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「工匠在工坊里做活」——既能造梁，也能造谎

root: 源自拉丁语「工匠」及其「工坊、制作」的词族；诚实义指切割焊接，虚假义指编造与伪造；工匠一词更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one maker: material is cut and joined, chips are patterned, and stories are invented. The same word covers honest making and deliberate falsehood.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个制作者：材料被切割与连接，芯片被图形化，故事被编造。同一个词既覆盖诚实的制造，也覆盖有意的虚假。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat steel plate cut, ground and welded into a beam; the same gesture can also assemble a lie.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块平板钢被切割、打磨并焊成梁；同一个动作也能拼出一个谎言。

branches.en: THE HONEST CORE: cutting, forming and joining material into a member.
branches.cn: 诚实核心：把材料切割、成形并连接成构件。

branches.en: THE FALSEHOOD VERSION: inventing a story, and the invented thing itself.
branches.cn: 虚假版本：编造说法，以及被编造出来的东西。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT VERSION: deliberate forgery of paper or evidence.
branches.cn: 文书版本：有意伪造文件或证据。

branches.en: THE CHIP VERSION: deposition, etching and patterning on a wafer.
branches.cn: 芯片版本：晶圆上的沉积、刻蚀与图形化。

branches.en: THE SHOP VERSION: steel structure work and the workshop that does it.
branches.cn: 车间版本：钢结构加工与从事加工的车间。

intro.en: The word is Latin: a craftsman, his workshop, the act of making there, and then a story made without material.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语：工匠、他的工坊、在那里制作的行为，以及随后不用材料造出的故事。

latinIntro.en: Latin faber, fabrica and fabricatio supply the whole family, including fabric and prefabricate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的工匠、工坊与制作提供了整个词族，包括织物与预制。

items.example: The root of the whole family.

items.exampleCN: 它还给英语提供了「织物」。

items.example: It marks the process and the product.
The agent ending names the person or firm.
A narrowed descendant of the workshop word.
The compound keeps the honest sense only.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词只保留诚实义。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「工坊制作」进入英语，义为「制造；编造」
由「制造」加已然词尾构成，义为「制造的；捏造的」
由「制造」加施动词尾构成，义为「加工商」
由拉丁语「工坊」缩小而来，义为「织物」
由「预先」加「制造」构成，义为「预制」
由「预制」加名词词尾构成，义为「预制加工」

definition_zh: n. 占星术（以天体位置推断人事的信仰体系）；某一具体的占星传统
definition_en: The belief system that reads the positions of stars and planets as signs of human character and events; also one particular tradition of that practice.
core_image: 十二个符号围成一圈，把人的命运挂在星位上
scene: 她一边吃早饭一边看报纸角落的星座运势。 She reads the astrology column over breakfast.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：astrology 指以星象推断人事的那套信仰体系，即占星术。

senses.title: The practice of reading stars
senses.definition: the belief that star and planet positions reveal character and foretell events, treated as one body of practice
senses.definitionCN: 认为星体位置揭示性格并预示事件的信仰，作为一整套术来看待
senses.example: Astrology has no support from controlled tests.
senses.exampleCN: 占星术得不到对照试验的支持。
senses.why: The ending -logy once meant any account of a subject, so the word claimed the same standing as a science.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -logy 曾指任何一门关于某主题的记述，所以这个词一度自称与科学同等地位。

senses.title: One tradition of that practice
senses.definition: a particular system with its own signs and rules, such as Western or Chinese astrology
senses.definitionCN: 有自己符号与规则的某一体系，如西方占星或中国占星
senses.example: The two astrologies use different animal cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种占星传统使用不同的生肖循环。
senses.why: Once the practice spread across cultures, the noun became countable, naming each system separately.
senses.whyCN: 这套术跨文化传播后，名词变得可数，用来分别指称各个体系。

intro.en: Astrology is Greek astrologia, from aster, star, and logos, account: an account of the stars, a term that once covered astronomy as well.
intro.cn: astrology 就是希腊语 astrologia，由 aster「星」与 logos「记述」构成：关于星的记述，这个术语曾把天文学也包括在内。

items.en: Greek aster meant star, and gives every member of this word family its first half.
items.cn: 希腊语 aster 意为「星」，给这个词族的每个成员提供前半部分。

items.en: Greek logos meant word, reason or account, the ending that later came to mean a field of study.
items.cn: 希腊语 logos 意为「言说、理性、记述」，这个后缀后来表示一门学问。

items.en: In Greek the compound covered both careful observation of the heavens and interpretation of their meaning.
items.cn: 在希腊语中，这个复合词同时涵盖对天象的细致观测与对其含义的解读。

items.en: Latin kept the double sense, so medieval writers used it for what we now call astronomy.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留了双重含义，所以中世纪作者用它指今天所说的天文学。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century, still covering both measurement and divination.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词，当时仍兼指测量与占卜。

items.en: Seventeenth-century science kept astronomy for measurement and left astrology for the belief, fixing the modern contrast.
items.cn: 十七世纪的科学把「测量」留给 astronomy，把「信仰」留给 astrology，固定了今天的对立。

note.en: The look-alike group sets the science beside the belief and adds two other -logy fields; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring sign systems.
note.cn: 形近组把科学与信仰并置，并加上另外两门 -logy 学问；近义组列出邻近的符号体系。

entries.definition: The scientific study of celestial bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 对天体的科学研究。

entries.definition: Relating to the reading of stars.
entries.definitionCN: 与读星断事有关的。

entries.definition: The study of the earth and its rocks.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球与岩石的学问。

entries.definition: The study of religious belief.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宗教信仰的学问。

entries.definition: A reading drawn from star positions.
entries.definitionCN: 依星位排出的运势解读。

entries.definition: Any attempt to read hidden signs.
entries.definitionCN: 一切解读隐秘征兆的做法。

entries.definition: The band of twelve signs used in star reading.
entries.definitionCN: 读星所用的十二宫带。

entries.definition: Reading meaning into numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 把含义读进数字里的术。

normalIntro.en: Astrology is astro-, star, plus -logy, account: an account of the stars that claims to read human lives.
normalIntro.cn: astrology 就是 astro-「星」加 -logy「记述」：一份关于星的记述，却声称能读出人的命运。

normal.en: Astronomy measures, astrology interprets.
normal.cn: astronomy 测量，astrology 解读。

normal.en: Uncountable for the practice, plural for traditions.
normal.cn: 指这门术时不可数，指传统时可数。

normal.en: Astrologer and astrologist name the person.
normal.cn: astrologer 与 astrologist 指人。

normal.en: Astrological is the adjective.
normal.cn: astrological 是形容词。

normal.en: The two words were one until the 1600s.
normal.cn: 这两个词在十七世纪前本是一个。

abstract.en: Picture twelve signs arranged in a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象十二个符号围成一圈。

abstract.en: Imagine a newspaper corner predicting your week.
abstract.cn: 想象报纸一角预测你这一周。

abstract.en: Think of a birth moment turned into a chart.
abstract.cn: 想象一个出生时刻被排成一张盘。

examples.en: She studies astrology as a hobby.
examples.cn: 她把占星当爱好来研习。

examples.en: Astrology was once part of university teaching.
examples.cn: 占星术曾是大学教学的一部分。

examples.en: The book compares several astrologies.
examples.cn: 这本书比较了几种占星传统。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：astro「星」+ -logy「学问」——把星象当成一门学问来读人事，就是占星术 astrology。

root: 希腊语 aster「星」加 logos「记述」构成 astrologia，经拉丁语入十四世纪英语，原兼指天象测量与占卜；十七世纪分家后专指占星信仰。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are one practice seen twice: the whole belief system, and each cultural version of it with its own signs.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一套术被看了两遍：整个信仰体系，以及各有符号的文化版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: twelve signs in a ring, a life hung on star positions
core.cn: 核心意象：十二个符号围成一圈，把人的命运挂在星位上

branches.en: A newspaper column predicting a week.
branches.cn: 预测一周运势的报纸专栏。

branches.en: A birth moment turned into a chart.
branches.cn: 被排成星盘的出生时刻。

branches.en: Twelve animals in one tradition.
branches.cn: 某一传统里的十二种动物。

branches.en: Two systems, different cycles.
branches.cn: 两套体系，不同的循环。

branches.en: Reading meaning into the sky.
branches.cn: 把含义读进天空里。

intro.en: Astrology is astro- plus -logy; the same ending builds geology, theology and numerology, while astronomy took -nomy instead.
intro.cn: astrology 是 astro- 加 -logy；同一后缀构成 geology、theology 与 numerology，而 astronomy 改用 -nomy。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is Greek aster, star, and logos, account, matched by Latin astrum and ratio; astrologia held both senses.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是希腊语 aster「星」与 logos「记述」，对应拉丁语 astrum 与 ratio；astrologia 曾兼含两义。

latinEntries.exampleCN: ratio 产生 reason 与 ration。

definition_zh: 主观性；主体性；主观感受
definition_en: the quality of belonging to a particular person's experience, perspective or judgment rather than to an independent external fact
core_image: 同一幅画前两位观者各写一页感受，一个说暖，一个说冷，画框始终不动
scene: 同一幅画前，两位观者各自写下看到的东西，一个说暖，一个说冷，画框始终不动。 Subjectivity enters when two readers describe the same page in opposite ways.
sceneCN: 这里指个人感受与视角的介入（第 1 个义项：属于个人经验的主观性）；句意为当两位读者用相反的方式描述同一页时，主观性就进来了。图中可辨识物件：画框、两页笔记、两支笔、观者、同一幅画。

pos.zh: 主观性；主体性；主观感受

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 subjectum 经法语而来，义为「主体；对象；使服从」
由该名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「主观的」
由主观形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「主观地」
由该名词加表示「使成为」的动词词尾再加名词词尾构成，义为「主体化」

senses.title: A particular person's experience
senses.definition: the quality of an experience as it is lived from one person's point of view and not as it is measured from outside
senses.definitionCN: 经验从某一个人的角度被经历、而非从外部被测量的性质
senses.example: Subjectivity enters when two readers describe the same page in opposite ways.
senses.exampleCN: 当两位读者用相反的方式描述同一页时，主观性就进来了。
senses.why: Two people can face the same object and carry away different experiences, because experience is lived from inside a life.
senses.whyCN: 两个人面对同一物体，却带走不同的经验，因为经验是从某一段人生内部被经历的。

senses.title: A judgment shaped by personal preference
senses.titleCN: 受个人偏好影响的判断
senses.definition: a judgment in which taste, memory or interest plays a part that the judge may not fully see
senses.definitionCN: 品味、记忆或利益参与其中而判断者未必完全察觉的判断
senses.example: The choice of colour is subjective, while the size of the frame is not.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色的选择是主观的，而画框的尺寸不是。
senses.why: Preference is not a defect in every judgment; it becomes a problem only when it is presented as independent fact.
senses.whyCN: 偏好并非在所有判断里都是缺陷；只有当它被当作独立事实呈现时，才成为问题。

senses.title: The researcher's own presence in qualitative work
senses.titleCN: 定性研究中研究者自身的在场
senses.definition: the part played by the researcher's background, relationship and reactions in shaping what is noticed and asked
senses.definitionCN: 研究者的背景、关系与反应在决定注意什么、追问什么时所起的作用
senses.example: Qualitative work treats subjectivity as data to be documented rather than as noise to be removed.
senses.exampleCN: 定性工作把主观性当作需要记录的数据，而不是需要清除的噪声。
senses.why: The interviewer is one of the instruments, so the instrument's position must be described.
senses.whyCN: 访谈者本身就是工具之一，因此这件工具的位置必须被描述。

senses.title: Emotional and affective life
senses.definition: the felt side of experience, including mood, emotion and bodily sensation
senses.definitionCN: 经验中被感受到的一面，包括心情、情绪与身体感觉
senses.example: Pain is known through subjectivity as well as through a scale from one to ten.
senses.exampleCN: 疼痛既通过主观感受被认识，也通过一到十的评分被认识。
senses.why: A number can record the intensity of pain, but only the person can report what the pain is like.
senses.whyCN: 数字可以记录疼痛的强度，但只有本人能报告疼痛是什么感觉。

senses.title: The philosophical subject
senses.definition: the conscious self that experiences, thinks and acts, considered as the bearer of experience
senses.definitionCN: 作为经验、思考与行动承担者的有意识自我
senses.example: Philosophy asks how a subject can know anything beyond its own subjectivity.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学追问主体如何能认识自身主观性之外的东西。
senses.why: This sense is about the bearer of experience rather than about a person's opinions.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项讲的是经验的承担者，而不是某人的意见。

senses.title: The subjectivity of perception
senses.definition: the ways in which the senses select, organise and colour what is present
senses.definitionCN: 感官对在场之物进行选择、组织与着色
senses.example: Colour constancy is a reminder that perception has its own subjectivity.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色恒常性提醒我们，感知有自己的主观性。
senses.why: The eye is not a window but an organ with habits, and those habits enter every observation.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛不是窗户，而是有习惯的器官，而这些习惯进入每一次观察。

senses.title: The interpretive lens in analysis
senses.definition: the frame of meaning a person brings to reading a text, an action or a dataset
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在阅读文本、行为或数据集时带入的意义框架
senses.example: Two coders agreed on the words but differed in the subjectivity of their reading.
senses.exampleCN: 两位编码员对字面一致，却在解读的主观性上不同。
senses.why: Meaning is not stored in the text like an object in a box; it is assembled by a reader with a history.
senses.whyCN: 意义不像箱子里的物品那样存放在文本中，而是由带着历史的读者组装起来。

senses.title: Subjectivity and objectivity together
senses.titleCN: 主观性与客观性的关系
senses.definition: the relation in which subjective position is disclosed so that objective checking remains possible
senses.definitionCN: 公开主观位置从而使客观核查仍然可能的关系
senses.example: Subjectivity is not the opposite of rigor when it is named and examined.
senses.exampleCN: 当主观性被命名并接受检视时，它就不是严谨的对立面。
senses.why: The pair works like a scale and a hand: the hand must be visible for the reading to be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 这一对像秤与手：手必须看得见，读数才可信。

intro.en: Subjectivity comes from Latin subjectum, something placed under, from subicere, to place beneath. The abstract noun is modern.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 subjectum「被置于下方的东西」，源出 subicere「置于下面」；抽象名词是近代构成的。

items.en: Subicere meant to place under or subject, from sub- under and iacere to throw.
items.cn: subicere 意为置于下方或使服从，由 sub-「在下」与 iacere「抛」构成。

items.en: Subjectum named what lies beneath, whether a substance, a topic or a person under authority.
items.cn: subjectum 指位于下方的东西，无论是实体、主题还是受支配的人。

items.en: Medieval philosophy used subject for the bearer of qualities, and the word became the opposite of object.
items.cn: 中世纪哲学用 subject 指性质的承担者，这个词后来成为 object 的对立面。

items.en: Descartes and later thinkers made the subject the conscious self that thinks and experiences.
items.cn: 笛卡尔及后来的思想家把 subject 变成思考与经验的有意识自我。

items.en: The abstract noun appeared with modern philosophy and psychology; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 抽象名词随近代哲学与心理学出现；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Social research later adopted subjectivity as a named feature of the researcher's position rather than a simple error.
items.cn: 社会科学后来把主观性当作研究者位置的一种明确特征，而不是简单的错误。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like subjectivity; the second group names neighbouring ideas of personal position and interpretation.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 subjectivity 相近；第二组是与「个人位置、解释」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: A topic, a person under authority, or the conscious self.
entries.definitionCN: 指主题、受支配的人或有意识的自我。

entries.definition: Belonging to personal experience or judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于个人经验或判断的。

entries.definition: From the point of view of the person concerned.
entries.definitionCN: 指从当事人角度出发。

entries.definition: The state of being placed under control.
entries.definitionCN: 指被置于控制之下的状态。

entries.definition: A verb mood; it comes from a different Latin verb meaning to join under.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种动词语气；来自另一个意为「接在下面」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: A particular standpoint from which something is seen.
entries.definitionCN: 指观看某物的特定立足点。

entries.definition: The researcher's social location and its effect on the work.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究者的社会位置及其对研究的影响。

entries.definition: The meaning a reader or analyst draws from material.
entries.definitionCN: 指读者或分析者从材料中得出的意义。

entries.definition: A felt state such as fear, joy or grief.
entries.definitionCN: 指恐惧、喜悦或悲伤等被感受到的状态。

entries.definition: A systematic slant that distorts a judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 指使判断失真的系统性倾向。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Subjectum lies under, and objectivity throws something before; the two words face each other across the mind.
normal.cn: subjectum 位于下方，「客观性」却把某物抛到前方；两个词隔着一颗心灵相对。

normal.en: Subjectivity is not the same as bias: bias is a slant that can be corrected, subjectivity is a position that must be disclosed.
normal.cn: 主观性不等于偏差：偏差是可以纠正的斜线，主观性是必须公开的位置。

normal.en: Qualitative researchers write reflexive notes because their own presence is part of the instrument.
normal.cn: 定性研究者写反思笔记，因为他们自身的在场是工具的一部分。

normal.en: Pain has a number and a feeling, and the two are not substitutes.
normal.cn: 疼痛有一个数字，也有一种感觉，二者不能互相替代。

normal.en: Two coders can agree on every word and still read the passage differently.
normal.cn: 两位编码员可以对每个字都一致，却仍对段落有不同解读。

abstract.en: A perspective is not a prison unless it is presented as a window with no frame.
abstract.cn: 视角本身不是牢房，除非它被呈现为一扇没有边框的窗。

abstract.en: The reader brings the furniture of a lifetime into a room of three sentences.
abstract.cn: 读者把一生的家具搬进只有三句话的房间。

abstract.en: Subjectivity becomes trustworthy when it stops hiding and starts describing itself.
abstract.cn: 当主观性不再躲藏而开始描述自己时，它才变得可信。

examples.en: The paper describes researcher subjectivity as part of the evidence rather than as a defect.
examples.cn: 该论文把研究者的主观性描述为证据的一部分，而不是缺陷。

examples.en: Subjectivity of experience cannot be replaced by a laboratory reading.
examples.cn: 经验的主观性无法被实验室读数取代。

examples.en: Reflexive notes made the team's subjectivity visible to readers.
examples.cn: 反思笔记让团队的主观性对读者可见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「主体」加「性」——同一幅画，一人说暖、一人说冷；画不动，感受各自带着自己的位置：主观性。

root: 拉丁 subicere「置于下方」← sub-「在下」+ iacere「抛」，名词 subjectum「位于下方的东西」；中世纪指性质的承担者，近代哲学转为有意识的自我，十九世纪形成抽象名词 subjectivity。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from lived experience toward the analytic lens: personal experience, preference in judgment, the researcher's presence, emotional life, the philosophical subject, perception, interpretation, and the relation to objectivity.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从亲历经验走向分析视角：个人经验、判断中的偏好、研究者的在场、情绪生活、哲学主体、感知、解释，以及与客观性的关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two viewers stand before one unchanged painting and write opposite accounts of its warmth.
core.cn: 核心意象：两位观者站在同一幅未变的画前，写下相反的温度感受。

branches.en: THE LIVED INSIDE: experience and feeling as they are felt from within one life.
branches.cn: 亲历之内：从一段人生内部被经历的经验与感受。

branches.en: THE PREFERENCE: taste entering a judgment that may be presented as fact.
branches.cn: 偏好：品味进入一个可能被当作事实的判断。

branches.en: THE RESEARCHER'S LENS: presence in the field and the frame brought to interpretation.
branches.cn: 研究者的透镜：在现场的在场，以及带入解释的框架。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT AND THE SENSES: the conscious bearer, and perception with its own habits.
branches.cn: 主体与感官：有意识的承担者，以及带自身习惯的感知。

branches.en: THE PAIR WITH OBJECTIVITY: a named position that remains open to checking.
branches.cn: 与客观性成对：被命名的位置仍向核查开放。

intro.en: Subjectivity is a Latin-derived abstract noun built on subjective, which descends from subjectum.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁来源抽象名词，建立在「主观的」这一形容词之上，而该形容词又出自 subjectum。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- and iacere supply the placing beneath; subjectum supplies the noun; -ive and -ity are English endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sub- 与 iacere 提供「置于下方」的动作，subjectum 提供名词，形容词词尾与名词词尾完成抽象化。

items.example: It places the subject beneath qualities or authority.
items.exampleCN: 它把主体置于性质或权力之下。

items.example: The same verb lies behind object.
items.exampleCN: 同一个动词也藏在 object 背后。

items.structure: Latin verb from sub- plus iacere

items.meaning: a topic, a person under rule, or the self
items.example: English keeps several layers at once.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留数层含义。

items.example: The paired word uses the same verb with the opposite prefix.
items.exampleCN: 配对词用同一动词但相反前缀。

items.example: The term names subjectivity made explicit.
items.exampleCN: 这个术语指被明确说出的主观性。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 subjectum 经法语而来，义为「主体；对象；使服从」
由该名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「主观的」
由主观形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「主观地」
由主观形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「主观性」
由该名词加表示「使成为」的动词词尾再加名词词尾构成，义为「主体化」

definition_zh: 排泄；排泄作用；排泄物
definition_en: the process by which animals and plants remove waste substances from the body, or the waste so removed
core_image: 身体把用不上的废物筛出来，经管道排出体外
scene: 这里指「排泄」。 The kidneys control the excretion of urea and excess salts.
sceneCN: 这里 excretion 指「肾脏排泄」（第 3 个义项：肾脏把代谢废物滤出并随尿排走）；句意：肾脏控制尿素与多余盐分的排泄。图中可辨识物件：肾脏剖面、肾单位示意、输尿管、尿液收集瓶。

pos.zh: 排泄；排泄作用；排泄物（指过程时不可数，指具体的排出物时可用复数 excretions）

senses.title: Removal of waste
senses.definition: the general process by which an organism gets rid of waste products of metabolism
senses.definitionCN: 生物体清除代谢废物的总体过程
senses.example: Excretion is one of the basic functions of life.
senses.exampleCN: 排泄是生命的基本功能之一。
senses.why: Latin excernere meant 'to sift out'; the noun names the separating of what the body will not keep.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 excernere 意为「筛出」；这个名词命名的是把身体不保留的东西分离出去。

senses.title: The waste itself
senses.definition: the substance removed, such as urine, sweat or exhaled carbon dioxide
senses.definitionCN: 被排出的物质，如尿、汗或呼出的二氧化碳
senses.example: The study measured nitrogen in the excretions of the animals.
senses.exampleCN: 研究测量了这些动物排泄物中的氮。
senses.why: The action noun can stand for its product, a common metonymy in scientific English.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词可代指其产物，这是科学英语中常见的转喻。

senses.title: Renal excretion
senses.titleCN: 肾排泄：肾脏滤出并排出废物
senses.definition: the filtering of waste from blood by the kidneys and its removal in urine
senses.definitionCN: 肾脏从血液中滤出废物并随尿排走
senses.example: The kidneys control the excretion of urea and excess salts.
senses.exampleCN: 肾脏控制尿素与多余盐分的排泄。
senses.why: Physiology assigned the general word to its main organ, since the kidney is the body's chief sifting machine.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把这个通用词指派给主要器官，因为肾是身体最主要的「筛子」。

senses.title: Gut elimination
senses.titleCN: 肠道排出：未被吸收的残渣离开身体
senses.definition: the removal of undigested residue through the intestines as faeces
senses.definitionCN: 未被消化的残渣经肠道以粪便形式排出
senses.example: Excretion through the gut removes fibre the body cannot use.
senses.exampleCN: 经肠道排出带走了身体无法利用的纤维。
senses.why: Although physiologists sometimes separate egestion from excretion, everyday usage places both under the same word.
senses.whyCN: 生理学有时把排遗与排泄分开，但日常用法把两者都放在同一个词下。

senses.title: Skin and lung excretion
senses.titleCN: 皮肤与肺的排泄：汗与二氧化碳
senses.definition: loss of waste through skin, lungs or gills rather than the kidney
senses.definitionCN: 废物经皮肤、肺或鳃而非肾脏排出
senses.example: Water and salts leave the body by excretion through the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 水和盐通过皮肤的排泄离开身体。
senses.why: Comparative anatomy needed the word for several routes, not just urine.
senses.whyCN: 比较解剖学需要这个词覆盖多条途径，而不只是尿。

senses.title: Drug excretion
senses.titleCN: 药物排泄：药物离开体内的速度
senses.definition: in pharmacology, the removal of a drug or its metabolites from the body
senses.definitionCN: 药理学中指药物或其代谢物离开身体
senses.example: Renal excretion determines how long a drug stays in the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 肾排泄决定一种药物在血液中停留多久。
senses.why: Pharmacology borrowed the physiological term because clearance is measured as a rate of removal.
senses.whyCN: 药理学借用了生理学术语，因为清除率正是以排出速率来衡量的。

senses.title: Excretion rate
senses.titleCN: 排泄率：单位时间内排出的量
senses.definition: the amount of a substance removed per unit of time, often per minute or per day
senses.definitionCN: 单位时间内排出的物质量，常以每分钟或每天计
senses.example: The excretion rate of calcium rises at night.
senses.exampleCN: 钙的排泄率在夜间升高。
senses.why: Clinical measurement turned the process into a quantity that can be graphed.
senses.whyCN: 临床测量把过程变成一个可以画成曲线的量。

senses.title: Plant excretion
senses.titleCN: 植物排泄：排出盐分、水分与气体
senses.definition: in botany, the removal of surplus salts, water or gases by leaves, roots or glands
senses.definitionCN: 植物学中指叶片、根或腺体排出多余的盐、水或气体
senses.example: Salt excretion lets mangroves survive in salty soil.
senses.exampleCN: 泌盐作用让红树林能在盐渍土壤中生存。
senses.why: Botany extended the animal term to plants, which also sift out what they cannot store.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把这个动物学术语扩展到植物，因为植物同样会筛出自己无法储存的东西。

senses.title: Cellular excretion
senses.titleCN: 细胞排泄：代谢废物被运出细胞
senses.definition: the transport of metabolic waste out of a cell across its membrane
senses.definitionCN: 代谢废物跨细胞膜被运出细胞
senses.example: Cellular excretion keeps the cytoplasm from becoming toxic.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞排泄使细胞质不至于变得有毒。
senses.why: The word scales down to the cell, where the same sifting happens across a membrane.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以缩小到细胞尺度，同一种筛出于是发生在膜的两侧。

intro.en: Excretion comes from Latin excretio, built on excernere 'to sift out', from ex- 'out' and cernere 'to sift'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: excretion 出自拉丁 excretio，由 excernere「筛出」构成，而 excernere 来自 ex-「向外」与 cernere「筛」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Cernere meant 'to sift, to separate, to distinguish'. It also gives English discern and certain, because sifting is a kind of deciding.
items.cn: cernere 意为「筛、分开、辨别」。它也衍生出英语 discern 与 certain，因为筛选就是一种判定。

items.en: Excernere added ex- 'out': to sift out, to separate and remove. Classical Latin used it for bodily discharges as well as for sorting grain.
items.cn: excernere 加上 ex-「向外」：筛出、分出并清除。古典拉丁既用它指身体排出，也指筛谷。

items.en: Excretio, excretionis named the act of sifting out. The word stayed technical and uncommon in classical prose.
items.cn: excretio、excretionis 指筛出的动作。该词在古典散文中偏技术性，并不常用。

items.en: English excretion is recorded in the seventeenth century, first in medical writing about bodily waste.
items.cn: 英语 excretion 记录于 17 世纪，最早见于讨论身体废物的医学写作。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology fixed the term as the counterpart of secretion and gave it a measured rate, an organ and a cellular scale.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学把这个词固定为 secretion 的对立词，并为它配上了速率、器官与细胞尺度。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and the semantic split between excretion and secretion was settled by usage rather than by any single reformer.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与语义分野）：英语最早书证年代存疑；excretion 与 secretion 的分工是用法逐渐确定的，并非某位改革者一锤定音。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family that are easily confused with excretion; the second holds near-synonyms for getting waste out of the body.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、易与 excretion 混淆的词；第二组是「把废物排出体外」的近义词。

entries.definition: To remove waste from the body; the verb names the act, while excretion names the process or its product.
entries.definitionCN: 把废物排出体外；动词指动作，excretion 指过程或产物。

entries.definition: Relating to excretion, as in excretory system; it describes organs, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 与排泄有关，如排泄系统；它描述器官，不指过程。

entries.definition: The waste substances themselves, always plural in form; excretion can mean either the process or the waste.
entries.definitionCN: 指排出的废物本身，形式上总为复数；excretion 既可指过程也可指废物。

entries.definition: The release of substances the body makes for a purpose, such as hormones or milk; excretion removes what is not wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 身体为某种目的制造并释放物质，如激素或乳汁；excretion 排出的则是不需要的东西。

entries.definition: A broad word for getting rid of anything; excretion is the biological case of it.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指清除任何东西；excretion 是它在生物学中的具体情形。

entries.definition: The release of a substance from a body, machine or wound; it can be normal or pathological, unlike the neutral excretion.
entries.definitionCN: 物质从身体、机器或伤口释放出来；它可以是正常或病理的，而 excretion 是中性的。

entries.definition: The technical term for removing undigested food as faeces; some textbooks keep it apart from excretion.
entries.definitionCN: 把未消化食物以粪便形式排出的专业术语；一些教材把它与排泄分开。

entries.definition: The emptying of the bowels specifically; it is narrower and more concrete than excretion.
entries.definitionCN: 专指排空肠道；比 excretion 更窄、更具体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + cernere 'sift' + -tion: to sift out and remove.
normal.cn: ex-「向外」+ cernere「筛」+ -tion：筛出来并清除。

normal.en: The family runs excrete, excretory, excreta and excrement.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 excrete、excretory、excreta、excrement。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: renal excretion, excretion rate, drug excretion.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出场景：肾排泄、排泄率、药物排泄。

normal.en: secretion keeps what is useful; excretion removes what is not.
normal.cn: secretion 保留有用的，excretion 清除无用的。

normal.en: excreta is always plural; excretion can be uncountable.
normal.cn: excreta 总为复数；excretion 可以不可数。

abstract.en: Picture a sieve held over a bucket: small unwanted grains fall through, the rest stays.
abstract.cn: 想象一只筛子架在桶上：细小无用的颗粒落下去，其余留下。

abstract.en: Picture a kidney-shaped filter washing blood and sending waste down a tube.
abstract.cn: 想象一只肾形滤器冲洗血液，把废物送进管道。

abstract.en: Picture a mangrove leaf with salt crystals shining on its surface.
abstract.cn: 想象一片红树林叶子，表面闪着盐晶。

examples.en: Excretion of carbon dioxide rises during exercise.
examples.cn: 运动时二氧化碳的排出量上升。

examples.en: The drug's excretion is slowed by kidney disease.
examples.cn: 肾病会减慢这种药物的排泄。

examples.en: Marine birds excrete salt through special glands.
examples.cn: 海鸟通过特殊的腺体排出盐分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex 向外 + cret 筛 + ion 过程」——把废物筛出体外 → excretion 排泄

root: 拉丁 ex-「向外」+ cernere「筛」→ excernere「筛出」→ excretio「排出」→ 英语 excretion。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one movement: a body sifts out what it cannot use, and that sifting can be named as a process, as the waste, as an organ's task, as a rate, or as something a plant or a cell also does.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：身体把用不上的东西筛出去，而这次筛出可被命名为过程、被命名为废物、被命名为某个器官的职责、被命名为一个速率，也可被命名为植物或细胞同样会做的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sieve that lets unwanted material pass out of the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只筛子，让不需要的物质离开身体。

branches.en: PROCESS AND PRODUCT: one noun covers both the sifting and the stuff that is sifted out.
branches.cn: 过程与产物：同一个名词既指筛出动作，也指被筛出的东西。

branches.en: TWO EXITS: the kidney filters blood, while the gut carries away what was never absorbed.
branches.cn: 两条出口：肾过滤血液，肠道带走从未被吸收的部分。

branches.en: OTHER SURFACES: skin, lungs and gills also remove waste, so the word is not tied to urine.
branches.cn: 其他表面：皮肤、肺与鳃也排出废物，因此这个词并不只与尿绑定。

branches.en: THE CLINICAL NUMBER: pharmacology asks how fast a drug leaves, and physiology turns the process into a rate.
branches.cn: 临床数字：药理学问药物多快离开，生理学把过程变成一个速率。

branches.en: LIFE AT EVERY SCALE: mangroves excrete salt through leaves, and a single cell excretes waste across its membrane.
branches.cn: 各尺度的生命：红树林经叶片排盐，单个细胞则跨膜排出废物。

intro.en: Excretion is a Latin verb of sifting plus a noun of action: ex- + cernere + -tio.
intro.cn: excretion 是拉丁「筛出」动词加动作名词后缀：ex- + cernere + -tio。

latinIntro.en: Latin excernere 'to sift out' yields excretio and excretus, hence English excrete, excretion, excretory and excreta; excrementum gives excrement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 excernere「筛出」产生 excretio 与 excretus，因此有英语 excrete、excretion、excretory、excreta；excrementum 则给出 excrement。

items.example: Excretion keeps the internal environment stable.

items.example: Samples of excreta were collected for analysis.

items.example: The pens are cleaned of excrement daily.

items.exampleCN: 盐腺内衬着具排泄作用的组织。

definition_zh: 依赖；取决于；依靠（某物或某人）才能存在、运作或成立
definition_en: to need something in order to exist, work or be decided, or to be controlled by it
core_image: 一盏吊灯悬在一根细链上，链子的另一端固定在房梁，灯下没有别的东西支撑
scene: 屋梁上垂下一根细链，吊灯全靠它悬着，灯下没有任何支撑。 The whole ceiling will be dependent on that single beam.
sceneCN: 这里指整片顶棚都靠那根梁承托（第 1 个义项：依靠某物才能成立）；句意为整个顶棚都将依赖于那一根梁。图中可辨识物件：房梁、细链、吊灯、空荡的灯下。

pos.zh: 形容词短语：依赖；取决于

collocations.phrase: be dependent on a single supplier

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「悬挂于下」动词经法语而来，义为「依赖；取决于」
由该动词加名词尾构成，义为「依赖」
由该形容词加名词尾构成，义为「依赖关系；属地」
由该形容词转作名词，义为「受抚养者」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「独立的」

senses.title: Needing something to exist
senses.definition: to need a resource in order to survive or function
senses.definitionCN: 需要某种资源才能存活或运作
senses.example: The whole ceiling will be dependent on that single beam.
senses.exampleCN: 整个顶棚都将依赖那一根梁。
senses.why: The image is of a lamp hanging from a chain: remove the support and the thing falls.
senses.whyCN: 意象是吊灯挂在链上：抽掉支撑，东西就落下。

senses.title: Decided by a factor
senses.definition: used when an outcome is settled by another variable
senses.definitionCN: 结果由另一变量决定时使用
senses.example: The final yield will be dependent on rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 最终产量将取决于降雨。
senses.why: Here dependence is logical rather than physical: one value fixes another.
senses.whyCN: 这里的依赖是逻辑性的：一个数值定住另一个。

senses.title: Relying on a person
senses.definition: used when someone needs another person's help or income
senses.definitionCN: 需要他人帮助或收入时使用
senses.example: Many students can be dependent on part-time work.
senses.exampleCN: 许多学生可能要靠兼职工作。
senses.why: Personal dependence often carries a social judgement, so the phrase appears in policy writing.
senses.whyCN: 人身依赖常带社会评判，因此短语多见于政策文字。

senses.title: Subordinate in status
senses.definition: used when a territory or body is governed by another
senses.definitionCN: 属地或机构受另一方治理时使用
senses.example: The smaller islands will be dependent on the mainland for fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 较小的岛屿将依赖大陆供应燃料。
senses.why: A territory under another's supply chain hangs from that support, as the beam image shows.
senses.whyCN: 属地靠他方供应链支撑，正如横梁意象所示。

senses.title: Controlled by a substance or mood
senses.definition: used when a person's state is controlled by a substance or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 人的状态受某种物质或情绪控制时使用
senses.example: Patients can be dependent on pain relief after long treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 长期治疗后病人可能依赖止痛药。
senses.why: Here the support is chemical: the body comes to need it in order to function.
senses.whyCN: 这里的支撑是化学性的：身体为了运转而离不开它。

senses.title: A variable in mathematics
senses.titleCN: 数学与统计中的变量依赖
senses.definition: used when one quantity changes according to another
senses.definitionCN: 一个量随另一个量变化时使用
senses.example: The measured value will be dependent on the starting temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 测量值将取决于起始温度。
senses.why: Statistics speaks of a dependent variable, the one that moves in response.
senses.whyCN: 统计学讲「因变量」，即随之变动的那个量。

senses.title: A system's reliance on a component
senses.definition: used when a machine or network cannot work without a part
senses.definitionCN: 机器或网络缺少某部件就无法工作时使用
senses.example: The network will be dependent on a single server.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网络将依赖一台服务器。
senses.why: Remove the server and the network stops, exactly like removing the chain.
senses.whyCN: 抽走服务器网络就停摆，正如抽走链条。

senses.title: Conditioned on circumstances
senses.definition: used when a plan holds only under certain conditions
senses.definitionCN: 计划只在特定条件下成立时使用
senses.example: The schedule can be dependent on the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 日程可能取决于天气。
senses.why: Weather is the condition the plan hangs on, so the frame is conditional.
senses.whyCN: 天气是计划所悬挂的条件，因此框架带条件意味。

intro.en: Depend comes from Latin dependere, to hang down or hang from, from de-, down, and pendere, to hang. The adjective came through French dépendant. The frame with on is modern and its first date is approximate.
intro.cn: depend 源自拉丁语 dependere「垂下、悬挂于」，由 de-「向下」与 pendere「悬挂」构成。形容词经法语 dépendant 而来。与介词连用的框架属近代，首见年代为约数。

items.en: Pendere means to hang and also gives pendulum and pension.
items.cn: pendere 意为「悬挂」，也是 pendulum 与 pension 的根基。

items.en: The prefix de- means down, so the compound pictures something hanging from a support.
items.cn: 前缀 de- 意为「向下」，复合词画出某物自支撑垂下。

items.en: Dependere means to hang from or to be attached to something above.
items.cn: dependere 意为「悬挂于、附着于上方之物」。

items.en: French dépendre shifted the image to needing or being decided by.
items.cn: 法语 dépendre 把意象转向「需要」或「由……决定」。

items.en: English dependent keeps the participle shape and pairs with on or upon.
items.cn: 英语形容词保留分词形态，与介词连用。

items.en: The frame is modern; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这一框架属近代用法，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the root but changes the form or reverses the meaning; the second group holds other verbs of reliance.
note.cn: 第一组共用词根而改变形式或反转意义；第二组是其他表示依靠的动词。

entries.definition: The verb states reliance directly and is less formal than the adjective frame.
entries.definitionCN: 动词更直接陈述依赖，也不如形容词框架正式。

entries.definition: Upon is the formal alternative to on in older prose.
entries.definitionCN: upon 是 on 的书面替代，多见于较早文字。

entries.definition: The negative form marks freedom from control, with a different preposition.
entries.definitionCN: 否定形式表示不受控制，介词也不同。

entries.definition: The noun names the relation, or a territory governed by another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指依赖关系，或受他方治理的属地。

entries.definition: It adds trust to need, and often takes a person.
entries.definitionCN: 它在「需要」之外加上「信任」，常接人。

entries.definition: It stresses that an outcome holds only if a condition holds.
entries.definitionCN: 它强调结果只在条件成立时才成立。

entries.definition: It pictures a door turning on a hinge, so the factor is decisive.
entries.definitionCN: 它画出门绕铰链转动，因此该因素具有决定性。

entries.definition: It is the legal and contractual way to state a precondition.
entries.definitionCN: 它是法律与合同里陈述前提条件的方式。

normalIntro.en: The normal associations use the real hanging image, the verb-adjective pair and the independent opposite.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的悬挂意象、动词与形容词配对以及「独立」的反面。

normal.en: Pendere is to hang, so dependence is hanging from a support.
normal.cn: 词根意为「悬挂」，依赖就是挂在支撑上。

normal.en: Remove the beam and the lamp falls: that is the test of dependence.
normal.cn: 抽掉梁，灯就落下：这是依赖的检验。

normal.en: The verb depend on is plainer; the adjective frame is more formal.
normal.cn: 动词形更朴素，形容词框架更正式。

normal.en: Independent takes of, not on, because the direction reverses.
normal.cn: 「独立的」用另一介词，因为方向反转。

normal.en: Statistics calls the moving quantity the dependent variable.
normal.cn: 统计学把随之变动的量称作因变量。

abstract.en: Like a lamp hanging from one thin chain with nothing beneath it.
abstract.cn: 像吊灯只靠一根细链悬着，下方空无一物。

abstract.en: Like a row of dominoes waiting for the first push.
abstract.cn: 像一排骨牌，等着第一推。

abstract.en: Like a plant whose roots reach one thin layer of water.
abstract.cn: 像根系只够到一层薄水的植物。

examples.en: The whole ceiling will be dependent on that single beam.
examples.cn: 整个顶棚都将依赖那一根梁。

examples.en: The final yield will be dependent on rainfall.
examples.cn: 最终产量将取决于降雨。

examples.en: The schedule can be dependent on the weather.
examples.cn: 日程可能取决于天气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「比 迪彭登特 昂」——屋梁垂下细链，吊灯全靠它悬着：依赖；取决于
